title: Resolution: clauses and finite refutations
summary: Use one inference rule on clauses, prove refutational completeness by eliminating atoms, and obtain a finite satisfiability procedure.
abstract: Can a single inference rule find every contradiction among propositional requirements? Resolution combines two clauses, each a finite collection of alternatives, by removing one opposing pair. Starting from requirements such as “at least one switch is on” and “each switch is off,” it builds a finite proof ending in the empty clause, which has no possible true alternative. We prove that this rule preserves truth and can refute every finite unsatisfiable collection of clauses. This also gives a terminating proof search and a way to establish a propositional formula by refuting its negation.
